title: Raise the contract.test.ts manifest-example timeout so CI load cannot fail the Check gate
description: Raised by the ward-cli worker on 2026-10-26 from the WCLI-82 release cut, at the lead ruling that it is filed outside opum-ai/ward-cli#188 and the test is not changed there. MEASURED: the Check job failed on 36e9514 with "manifest > every example emits a declared kind and a declared exit code" taking 5401ms against bun test default 5000ms ceiling. It is not an assertion failure - the same test passes in 592ms in isolation on the developer machine, and a re-run of the failed job on the same SHA passed 9 of 9. The full suite on the self-hosted runner takes ~35s against ~25s locally, so the per-test ceiling is being hit by runner load, not by the test getting slower. WHY IT MATTERS: Check is a required check on dev, so a timeout fails the merge, and it will most likely fire during the release cut when the tree is busy. It is not a release blocker - a re-run of the failed job is the remedy - but every occurrence costs a cycle. SCOPE: raise that one test per-test timeout, or reduce its cost, so it cannot lose a race against suite-wide load. Do not weaken or delete the assertion: it is the check that every manifest example emits a declared kind and a declared exit code, which is what keeps the command contract honest. Note the constraint from the repository own rules: a test that asserts a wall-clock bound must assert it, not wait it out, and a ceiling parked at the harness timeout can never fire - the fix here is the opposite direction, a ceiling with headroom over the slowest measured run.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A full bun test run on the self-hosted Linux ARM64 runner passes the manifest-example test without a re-run, at a commit whose only change is this task, evidenced by a green Check run on that commit.

The test still asserts what it asserted before: every manifest example emits a declared kind and a declared exit code. The timeout is the only thing that changes, so no assertion is weakened, skipped or removed.
The ceiling chosen is recorded with the measurement it came from, so the next person can tell whether it still has headroom rather than re-deriving it.
